title: Giving Premium Relief Back on a Ridgecrest Advantage Plan Premium Account
content:
Where more plan premium has been charged on the premium account of a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment than the member is liable for, because the low income premium subsidy the member has been awarded reduces the plan premium of a plan that carries prescription drug coverage while the full premium is still charged, the plan gives the difference back to the member as premium relief on that account.

The relief is given back by posting one credit entry against a single plan premium charge already standing on the account. The representative posts it on the member's behalf. The charge itself is left standing at its full amount, and what the member owes becomes the charge less the credits posted against it. Afterwards the new credit is visible on the member's premium account, and the member can be told the reference number of the entry and the amount given back.

### How the entry is made

The tool `post_premium_relief_credit_3acf64b3` is first unlocked and then called by the representative on the member's behalf.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `advantage_enrollment_id` | The reference number of the Medicare Advantage enrollment whose premium account is credited, read from the member's enrollment record before the call | An identifier |
| `source_premium_entry_id` | The reference number of the single plan premium charge entry this credit relieves, read from the premium account of that enrollment before the call | An identifier |
| `credit_amount` | The money given back on the premium account, in USD | A decimal number carried to 2 decimal places, rounded half away from zero to the nearest cent at the moment it is passed; never negative, and an empty value is not accepted |
| `adjustment_reason_code` | Why the credit is being granted | Exactly one of the literals listed below |

The complete set of literals `adjustment_reason_code` accepts:

- `not_applicable` — the entry is not a credit at all, so no reason is carried;
- `retroactive_rate_change` — the plan premium for coverage months already billed has been restated after the fact;
- `duplicate_payment_refund` — the member's money reached the plan twice for the same coverage month and the surplus is handed back;
- `cms_retroactive_disenrollment` — CMS has ended the coverage with effect from a date already billed;
- `low_income_subsidy_premium_reduction` — the member has been awarded a low income premium subsidy, so the subsidised part of the plan premium is given back;
- `billing_error_correction` — the plan raised the charge wrongly in the first place;
- `part_b_premium_reduction` — the entry carries a Part B premium reduction handled through Social Security.

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the reference number the plan has assigned to the new credit entry, a string beginning `apc`, the amount credited written to two decimal places in USD, the coverage month the credit belongs to as YYYY-MM, and the reference number of the plan premium charge it relieves. The sentence is returned only when the entry has been booked on the premium account, so its presence is what indicates the call completed.

### What the entry records of itself

The entry records, from the size of the credit against the size of the charge, whether part of that charge is left outstanding, whether it is settled exactly, or whether the credit goes beyond it.
